De acuerdo con La Nación (Costa Rica), imágenes compartidas en medios y redes sociales muestran a decenas de policías y francotiradores en edificios de los alrededores. Según El Comercio (Perú), el presidente Abelardo de la Espriella informó que cinco mujeres mayores fueron liberadas de las 30 personas retenidas por delincuentes que intentaban asaltar un carro de valores en un supermercado de Cartagena. De acuerdo con Semana (Colombia), hombres armados y encapuchados ingresaron al establecimiento y tomaron como rehenes a varias personas.
stories.narrEn: According to Hindustan Times, the Rafael Nunez airport in Cartagena briefly stopped incoming flights as the armed forces used one of its runways in connection with the incident. According to France 24, armed robbers took roughly two dozen people hostage at a supermarket in Colombia’s tourist city of Cartagena on Tuesday, prompting a major police operation and a temporary suspension of incoming flights, authorities said. According to The Guardian, police say group seized store in city of Cartagena and local media showed footage of snipers on nearby buildings A group of armed men with their faces covered seized a supermarket in the Colombian city of Cartagena on Tuesday and are holding 25 people hostage, the president, Abelardo de la Espriella, said on Tuesday.

stories.narrEn: NewsBTC reports: Key takeaways BlackRock has launched its first tokenized money market fund in Asia-Pacific, the HKD Digital Liquidity Fund, for investors in Hong Kong. According to The Defiant, the HKD Digital Liquidity Fund offers tokenized units from HK$10, but its stablecoin payment route is for professional investors. According to Cointelegraph, the tokenized fund launched with approximately $100 million in assets, with Standard Chartered and Ant International participating as seed investors. According to CoinGape, the fund notably allows subscribers to invest using stablecoins, while it is similar to an earlier-launched tokenized money market fund in the U.S., which could serve as a reserve asset for stablecoin issuers.

stories.narrEn: CoinGape reports: American Bitcoin, the Bitcoin mining company co-founded by Eric Trump, has secured a $150 million revolving credit facility from crypto brokerage FalconX. According to Cointelegraph, the miner can borrow against its Bitcoin to fund operations and expansion after selling about 465 BTC to cover expenses in the third quarter. According to CoinDesk, the Nasdaq-listed crypto miner can borrow without selling its reserves or issuing new shares, but falling BTC prices could force it to pledge more collateral. According to CryptoSlate, the miner reported no draws as of Nov. 23, and FalconX can demand more bitcoin if collateral falls below the contract’s margin-call threshold.
